title: The Book of Daniel (Cambridge Bible for Schools and Colleges)

verification_log.method: Downloaded and read the OCR text, pp. 84–107

pp. 94–98: table of the "Roman" (A) and "Grecian" (B) theories; A first in 2 Esdras 12:11, then Barnabas, Hippolytus, the Fathers, Auberlen, Hengstenberg, Keil, Pusey; papal (Rule 1869) and futurist variants; Driver's objection that no ten kingdoms arise from Rome; pp. 98–102: B first in Ephrem Syrus, then Ewald, Bleek, Delitzsch, Kuenen, Bevan; little horn of ch. 7 = that of ch. 8 (Antiochus); time, times, half = 3½ years as in 12:7; candidate Seleucid lists for the ten horns; pp. 102–107: "one like a son of man" = ideal Israel (vv. 18, 22, 27), messianic reading early (Similitudes of Enoch)

Introduction pp. x–xi: the image signifies four empires, "in all probability the Median, Persian, and Greek" after Babylon, the stone = the kingdom of God; p. lxxxvii: the kingdom of God follows "immediately upon the overthrow of the 'fourth empire' in the person of Antiochus Epiphanes"
